ALGER, 25/06/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Dans: ALGIERS, 06/25/2026 (Algeria Tech) — In the wilaya of Saïda, Algérie Télécom has transformed an abandoned building into a center of excellence dedicated to digital skills training. The infrastructure, operational as of June 14, 2026, will welcome thousands of young people free of charge for modern technology training sessions.
Inauguration du plus grand centre de com: Inauguration of the largest digital skills center in the wilaya of Saïda
La wilaya de Saïda se dote désormais d’u: The wilaya of Saïda now has a strategic tool for the professional integration of youth thanks to the rehabilitation of an abandoned building into a digital skills training center. Named the Saïda Digital Skills Center, this 1,200 m² space, fully redesigned by the Algérie Télécom teams, will be operational starting June 14, 2026. It will offer free training in web development, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, digital project management, and other digital professions, in partnership with the National Agency for the Promotion of ICT (ANPT) and local stakeholders. The center will feature 15 rooms equipped with 300 computer workstations, a 100-seat amphitheater, and a coworking space. According to initial estimates, it will be able to accommodate up to 5,000 beneficiaries per year, with a targeted professional integration rate of 70% within 12 months following the training.
Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la dynam: This initiative is part of the national momentum of digitalization and youth unemployment reduction, with a total budget of 350 million Algerian dinars allocated by the State for rehabilitation and equipment. The wali of Saïda, Mr. Mohamed Lamine Belhocine, praised the commitment of Algérie Télécom and local authorities, emphasizing that this project "responds to an urgent demand from the region's youth, who are often forced to migrate to large cities for training." The first training sessions, scheduled for September 2026, will primarily target unemployed graduates and innovative project holders.
Ce projet illustre la volonté des pouvoi: This project illustrates the public authorities' determination to turn peripheral wilayas into technological development hubs, breaking away from the historical concentration of digital infrastructure in major metropolitan areas like Algiers or Oran. With a youth unemployment rate exceeding 28% nationwide, according to the latest data from the National Office of Statistics (ONS), this center represents a concrete response to regional disparities in access to qualifying training. The skills acquired in this type of facility could help reduce brain drain by offering local opportunities to Algerian talents.
Sur le plan économique, l’impact pourrai: Economically, the impact could be substantial: a recent World Bank study estimates that each ICT training project generates a return on investment of 4 to 6 times its initial cost, thanks to the creation of direct and indirect jobs. For the wilaya of Saïda, this would translate into a drop in the local unemployment rate and increased attractiveness for investors, particularly in the agri-food and digital services sectors. Furthermore, this model could be replicated in other wilayas, building on the network of 48 Employment and Competitiveness Houses already deployed by the ANPT.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
L’Algérie compte actuellement 58 wilayas: Algeria currently has 58 wilayas, 30 of which now have a digital skills training center, thanks to partnerships between the State, Algérie Télécom, and private operators like Mobilis, Djezzy, and Ooredoo. With a mobile penetration rate exceeding 125% in 2025 (nearly 55 million subscribers for a population of 45 million), the country boasts one of the highest rates in Africa. The number of fixed and mobile internet subscribers reached 32 million in 2026, according to the latest data from the Postal and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE), representing an annual growth of 8%.
Le Plan Numérique 2030, lancé en 2021, v: The Digital Plan 2030, launched in 2021, aims to position Algeria as a regional technology hub, with public and private investments estimated at 2,000 billion dinars. Algérie Télécom, the sector leader, has already deployed 40,000 km of fiber optics and plans to reach 90% national coverage by 2027. Meanwhile, ARPCE has refocused its missions on supporting startups and regulating 5G services, with the first commercial tests expected by the end of 2026. These initiatives rely on a booming ecosystem, with over 1,200 active startups in ICT, according to the annual report of the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.
M. Mohamed Lamine Belhocine, wali de la: Mr. Mohamed Lamine Belhocine, wali of the wilaya of Saïda: "This center is a response to the social and economic emergency affecting our youth. Thanks to this initiative, we are offering a credible alternative to migration to big cities, while strengthening Saïda's attractiveness for investors."
M. Kamel Benmahmoud, ministre de la Post: Mr. Kamel Benmahmoud, Minister of Post and Telecommunications: "Projects like this are part of the President of the Republic's vision to make ICT a lever for inclusive development. We intend to extend this model to all wilayas by 2028."
M. Nadir Larbaoui, PDG d’Algérie Télécom: Mr. Nadir Larbaoui, CEO of Algérie Télécom: "This center symbolizes our commitment to reducing the digital divide and training a generation of talents capable of competing with international standards. We have mobilized our best teams to guarantee quality support."
Le Centre de Compétences Numériques de S: The Saïda Digital Competencies Center will serve as a model for the remaining 28 wilayas still lacking similar infrastructure. By the end of 2026, three other wilayas (Tlemcen, Béchar, and Bordj Bou Arréridj) are expected to inaugurate comparable centers, with an overall budget of 1.2 billion dinars. At the same time, ANPT and Algérie Télécom are finalizing a partnership with the Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie (AUF) to certify the training provided in these centers, in collaboration with Algerian and European universities.
À moyen terme, le ministère de la Poste: In the medium term, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications plans to create a national network of Digital Competencies Centers, interconnected via a dedicated digital platform. The objective is to enable beneficiaries to follow hybrid training paths (in-person and online) and access targeted job offers via a national skills exchange. A pilot phase is planned for 2027, with gradual rollout by 2030, in line with the objectives of the Digital Plan 2030.
